name: swift-yyjson (YYJSON)
verdict_reason: The raw results confirm 8.7x-15x faster untyped parsing than JSONSerialization on four standard fixtures. The headline table overstates canada.json (~16x claimed, raw p50 about 9.5x), and no numbers are published for its JSONDecoder replacement against Codable JSONDecoder.
tier_reason: Benchmark source is public (swift-yyjson-benchmark, package-benchmark) and the raw output names the host (16 arm64 cores, 48 GB) and its Darwin 25.2.0 kernel; first-party.
claimed_speedup: p50 wall clock, YYJSONValue parse vs JSONSerialization: twitter.json 128 μs vs 1962 μs (15.3x), citm_catalog.json 331 vs 3328 μs (10.1x), canada.json 1247 vs 11821 μs (9.5x), tokenizer.json 6521 vs 56951 μs (8.7x) (ratios derived from page data). README summary table: ~16×, ~10×, ~16×, ~9×. twitter.json: 3 allocations vs over 6,600; peak memory 19 MB vs 378 MB.
workload: Parsing four nativejson-benchmark fixtures (twitter.json ~632KB, citm_catalog.json ~1.7MB, canada.json ~2.2MB, tokenizer.json ~11MB) into an untyped value: YYJSONValue(data:) vs JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with:)
metric: time (p50 wall clock), allocations, peak memory
hardware: Apple silicon MacBook Pro, 16 arm64 cores, 48 GB (chip not named)
toolchain: swift package benchmark (package-benchmark); Swift version not stated
one_liner: yyjson wrapper with JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder-style APIs; parses 9-15x faster than JSONSerialization, Codable path unmeasured.
how_it_is_fast: yyjson parses the whole document into one contiguous immutable structure with a handful of allocations (3 for twitter.json) and fast floating-point parsing. YYJSONValue reads from that structure on demand instead of creating NSDictionary, NSArray and NSNumber objects for every node as JSONSerialization does. In-place parsing can reuse the input buffer for string storage.
use_it_when: Untyped JSON access (dictionary-style traversal, partial reads) on large documents
Memory-constrained parsing of large files: 19 MB vs 378 MB peak on twitter.json
skip_it_when: Your hot path is Codable decoding: no YYJSONDecoder vs JSONDecoder numbers are published
You need exact decimal semantics with the fast number strategy, which the README calls lossy (opt-in)
caveats: Baseline is JSONSerialization building a full Foundation object graph; YYJSONValue does not materialize Swift objects up front, so the comparison favors YYJSON when only part of the document is read.
Summary table and raw results disagree for canada.json: the table says ~36.0 ms vs ~2.3 ms, the raw p50 is 11821 μs vs 1247 μs.
Codable encoder/decoder benchmarks exist in the benchmark repo but their results are not published.
tradeoffs: The largest wins need the YYJSONValue API rather than the Codable drop-in

evidence.quote: Parsing twitter.json requires only 3 allocations compared to over 6,600 for Foundation, with peak memory of 19 MB versus up to 378 MB.
Host 'MacBook-Pro.local' with 16 'arm64' processors with 48 GB memory, running: Darwin Kernel Version 25.2.0
